summary: Report the requested harness launch exit promptly and pace short-lived automatic restarts

replay.detail: No canonical replay change or new replay trigger. Existing durable runtime.observed claims retain declaration evidence, and harness.diagnostic claims add fixed early-exit diagnostics. Launch waits read runtime-host-local receipts and those durable observations.

schema.detail: No database tables, indexes, migrations or schema version changes. Existing observation kinds and fields carry launch diagnostics, readiness receipts and retry deadlines.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes. Existing guarded effects and clock/due dependencies remain in use.

compatibility.detail: The updated agents new CLI uses a new agent-launch read route and authenticated host-relay operation for pinned early-exit evidence. Upgrade local and destination daemons for that evidence. If a daemon or relay returns 404/503, creation uses the prior readiness/event wait within the same timeout, retaining the selected declaration and first observed incarnation; this compatibility path cannot recover an unobserved early-exit code or output. It never claims remote replication from the local card. Older CLIs keep working with updated daemons. JSON creation results add stages and error fields; upgraded early-exit evidence returns the requested process status, including zero. Older peers reject the new peer operation.

downtime.detail: No additional service interruption beyond the normal binary deployment. No live daemon restart or fleet seat stimulus was used for validation.

manual.detail: Automatic short-lived agent retries wait from 5 seconds up to 120 seconds including deterministic jitter, using existing scheduler state. A stable 60-second lifetime, changed launch revision or explicit person retry resets the consecutive delay. Existing restart-intensity parking still applies. Use agents show for faults and retry explicitly after correcting setup; creation never attaches to a replacement incarnation.

recovery.detail: No forward-only migration. Binary swap-back remains supported with existing graph state; older binaries reject the added peer operation, while unknown JSON CLI fields are additive. Startup output uses bounded runtime-host-local SystemLocal receipts, served through signed fleet-peer transport without a separate per-agent ownership check. Replicated diagnostics, step failures and crash-loop faults contain fixed failure text; OTLP logs omit local startup detail. Credential and transcript markers withhold the captured local output window.
